parsed.explanation: Visitor-facing positives are substantial: no trans criminalisation, transphobia as an aggravating factor since 2017, hate-speech penalties, conversion-therapy ban, funded care, accepting mainstream society (pride, high acceptance figures), and oversight bodies that formally document problems. Against that, custody is a tier-1 exposure: placement by birth sex, isolation and strip-search persist unremedied through two inspection opinions (2010, 2021) and were confirmed current in the 2024–25 Louna case — institutional failure corroborating exposure, though it binds only a detained visitor. Border friction rests on a single dated 2017 account (scattered). The 2023 national survey (64% of trans people reporting identity-related discrimination) is recent, trans-specific evidence of everyday hostility without a working prohibition, with ombudsman guidance that is paper remedy. Regional variation is LGB-only and unquantified for trans travellers. Net: functioning protections and acceptance, offset by unremedied custody placement and documented service discrimination prevalence.
